newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent prisons agency not a new idea - Bruton.
newsitem.headline: Independent prisons agency not a new idea - Bruton.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton told parliament on Wednesday the Department of Justice had been working on the establishment of an independent prisons board for the past year.
The government also decided in principle some time ago to set up an independent courts services board, Bruton said.
He said it had been decided on Tuesday to proceed immediately with the creation of both of these boards.

The decision was announced on Tuesday at the beginning of a two-day debate on a no-confidence motion in the government, after an administrative blunder in the Department of Justice forced release and immediate re-arrest of 16 high-risk prisoners.
Opposition parties said the government's proposals were a knee-jerk reaction to the blunder.
The prisoners were freed after it was discovered that the judge who detained them should no longer have been working in Ireland's three-judge anti-subversive "special criminal court".
The judge had been officially removed from the court in August, but continued to work because Owen's justice ministry forgot to inform him of the decision.

Opposition parties have demanded Owen's resignation, but all three parties in the ruling coalition have pledged her their full support and the government is expected to survive Wednesday night's confidence vote.
